problemText: Simplify and write in standard form: (4x² + 3x - 7) + (2x² - 8x + 5)
hints: Combine like terms only — x² terms with x² terms, x terms with x terms, constants with constants.
The x terms are 3x and -8x. What is 3 - 8?

problemText: Simplify and write in standard form: (9x² - 4x + 6) - (3x² + 5x - 2)
hints: Rewrite the subtraction as adding the opposite: the minus flips the sign of ALL THREE terms in the second group.
After flipping you have 9x² - 4x + 6 - 3x² - 5x + 2. Note the last term became +2.
The monomial out front hits every term inside — all three of them, including the constant.
Multiply the coefficients and ADD the exponents: -3x² times 4x³ gives -12x⁵.
Four products, not two: First, Outer, Inner, Last.
Outer is 2x times 4 = 8x and Inner is -7 times 3x = -21x. Combine those two middle terms.

problemText: Multiply (4x + 3)(2x - 5), write the product in standard form, and type just the coefficient of the x term as a number.
hints: Only the Outer and Inner products carry a plain x.
Outer is 4x times -5 and Inner is 3 times 2x. Add those two coefficients.

problemText: Multiply and write in standard form: (x + 3)(2x² - 5x + 4)
hints: Six products in all: the x hits each of the three terms, then the 3 hits each of the three terms.
The x² terms are -5x² (from x times -5x) and +6x² (from 3 times 2x²). Combine them before you answer.
Squaring means (x + 7)(x + 7) — there is a middle term.
Use (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² with a = x and b = 7. The middle term is DOUBLE the product.
Use (a - b)² = a² - 2ab + b² with a = 3x and b = 8 — and square the coefficient too.
The last term is (-8)(-8), so it comes out positive.
Same two terms with opposite signs — that is the difference-of-squares shape.
FOIL if you want proof: the +30x and -30x middle terms cancel.
Use (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b², this time with a = 2x² and b = 5.
Squaring 2x² means squaring the 2 as well and doubling the exponent: (2x²)² = 4x⁴.

problemText: Use the difference-of-squares pattern to compute 62 × 58 without long multiplication. Type your answer as a number.
hints: Both numbers sit the same distance from a round number — find it.
They are each 2 away from 60, so this is (60 + 2)(60 - 2) = 60² - 2².
Expand each square separately first — they are NOT the same expression.
You get (4x² + 36x + 81) - (4x² - 36x + 81). The x² terms and the constants cancel; the middle terms do not.

problemText: Factor 10x² + 25x completely by pulling out the GREATEST common factor, so that nothing inside the parentheses can still be factored out.
hints: The GCF has a number part and a variable part: the largest integer dividing both coefficients, and the lowest power of x in both terms.
Pull out 5x, then divide each original term by 5x.

problemText: Factor 14x³ - 35x² + 7x completely by pulling out the GREATEST common factor, so that nothing inside the parentheses can still be factored out.
hints: Largest integer dividing 14, 35, and 7? Lowest power of x in all three terms?
The GCF is 7x. Watch the last term: 7x ÷ 7x = 1, and that 1 must be written.
Split into two pairs: (x³ + 4x²) + (3x + 12), then factor the GCF out of each pair.
The first pair gives x²(x + 4) and the second gives 3(x + 4). The matching parentheses are the shared factor.

problemText: Factor -18x³ + 24x² - 6x completely, pulling out a NEGATIVE greatest common factor so the leading coefficient inside the parentheses is positive.
hints: The size of the GCF is 6x; the problem asks you to take it out as -6x.
Dividing by a negative flips the sign of EVERY term inside, including the last one: -6x ÷ (-6x) = 1.

problemText: The greatest common factor of 20x⁴ - 45x³ + 15x² can be written as Ax^B, where A is a positive whole number and B is the exponent on x. Type the value of A + B as a single number.
hints: Number part: the largest integer that divides 20, 45, and 15.
Variable part: the LOWEST power of x that appears in every term.
Pair them up: (2x³ - 10x²) + (-3x + 15). Factor 2x² out of the first pair.
The second pair starts negative, so pull out -3, flipping both signs: -3(x - 5). Now both parentheses read (x - 5).
Find two numbers that multiply to 20 and add to 9.
Both the constant and the middle coefficient are positive, so both numbers are positive.
The constant is positive, so the two numbers share a sign — and that sign matches the middle coefficient.
Both are negative. Which negative pair multiplies to 24 and adds to -11?
The constant is negative, so the two numbers have opposite signs.
The one that is bigger in size takes the sign of the middle term, which is negative. Product 40, difference 3.
The leading coefficient is not 1, so use the ac-method: a·c = 2 × 12 = 24.
Two numbers with product 24 and sum 11 are 3 and 8. Split the middle term: 2x² + 3x + 8x + 12, then group.

problemText: Factor 6x² - 19x + 10 completely. One factor is (2x - 5) and the other is (3x + k). Type the value of k as a number.
hints: There is no common factor, so use the ac-method: a·c = 6 × 10 = 60.
Two numbers with product 60 and sum -19 are -15 and -4. Split: 6x² - 15x - 4x + 10, then group.
Take the greatest common factor out first — all three terms share it, and it stays in the final answer.
After pulling out 3x you are left with x² - x - 30. Two numbers with product -30 and sum -1.

choices: prime — it does not factor over the real numbers
hints: Two terms with a minus between them, and both terms are perfect squares.
Use a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b) with a = x and b = 7.
Square-root the WHOLE first term, coefficient included: what squares to 25x²?
With a = 5x and b = 8, apply a² - b² = (a + b)(a - b).
Three terms, and the first and last are perfect squares — test the perfect-square-trinomial pattern.
With a = x and b = 8, check that the middle term equals 2ab = 2 × x × 8. The middle sign tells you which binomial.

problemText: Factor 3x² - 75 completely over the real numbers, so that no factor can be broken down any further.
hints: Neither 3 nor 75 is a perfect square — pull out the common factor first and look again.
After factoring out 3 you have 3(x² - 25), and x² - 25 is still a difference of squares.

problemText: The trinomial 16x² - kx + 81 is a perfect-square trinomial that factors as (4x - 9)². Find the value of k and type your answer as a number.
hints: In a² - 2ab + b², the middle term is exactly 2 × a × b.
Here a = 4x and b = 9, and the stem already writes the middle term with a minus sign in front of k.

problemText: Factor 2x⁴ - 32 completely over the real numbers, so that no factor can be broken down any further.
hints: Pull out the common factor of 2 first, which leaves a difference of squares in x⁴ and 16.
That gives 2(x² + 4)(x² - 4) — but one of those two factors is itself a difference of squares. The other one is a sum of squares and is prime.
